The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 03-04-2023 at about 7-30 p.m. the petitioner was driving motor cycle bearing registration No.CTK-1756 from Byadarahalli towards Sigehalli, on Magadi main road, when he reached near Nice road junction, at that time driver of Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05/AH-1189 drove the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against road divider and came in reverse course and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.
Consequently, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that immediately the petitioner was shifted to Krishna Hospital,
Gollahatti, for first aid, then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, wherein, he was treated as an inpatient and discharged with advice for follow-up treatment.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment.

4. It is further stated that, at the time of accident the petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 21 years, he was a B.Com., student and also part time working as a supplier at Hotel and earning Rs.15,000/-
p.m.
On account of accidental injuries, the petitioner could not able to do his normal work as earlier and could not concentrate on his studies.
It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05/AH-1189.
Hence, the jurisdictional Kamakshipalya Traffic Police have registered a criminal case in Cr.No.98/2023 against the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal, remained absent, hence it was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 Insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.
6. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, it is contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further it has denied the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained, age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.
The respondent has admitted Nitish.L vs Balaagavi Traders on 9 July, 2025

It is the defense of the respondent No.2 that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.

Further contended that as per the MLC register from Sri Krishna Hospital, history of accident mentioned as "fall from bike by hitting divider", it is clear from the MLC register that the petitioner by colluding with the owner and the hospital authorities falsely implicated the vehicle for claiming compensation.
It is contended that the petitioner was solely responsible for the accident.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
It is also the contention of the respondent No.2 that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?
8. In order to substantiate the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
9. On the other hand, the respondent No.2- insurance company examined its Legal Executive as RW1 and got marked documents at Ex.R2 to Ex.R5.
Ex . R1 marked with consent

. 
10. Heard the arguments on both sides and the counsel for the petitioner has filed written arguments and also perused the materials available on record.
11.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,

 R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05/AH- Nitish.L vs Balaagavi Traders on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6479245/
3 1189, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
13.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but seriously disputed about involvement of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle remained absent and hence, he was placed exparte.

14. In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
15. In order to prove his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of his oral evidence has relied upon police documents as per Ex.P1 to P8 and Ex.P14.
Ex. P1

- true copy of the F.I.R. Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement, Ex.P3-true copy of the spot sketch, Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P5-true copy of the wound certificate, Ex.P6-true copy of the IMV report, Ex.P7-true copy of the charge sheet and Ex.P14-copy of police intimation.

16. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Kamakshipalya Traffic Police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
17.
On the contrary, the respondent No.2 in order to substantiate its case has examined Legal executive as RW1.

RW1 has deposed in his evidence that the alleged accident took place on 3.4.2023,
the complaint lodged on 4.4.2023, after lapse of one day.

Further deposed that as per MLC register from Sri Krishna Hospital history of accident mentioned as "Fall from bike by hitting divider", it is clear that insured TATA goods vehicle was falsely implicated for claiming compensation.

He has placed authorisation letter, policy copy, police intimation and wound certificate as pr Ex.R2 and Ex.R5.
18.
It is not in dispute that the accident in question was taken place on 3.4.2023 and the complaint was lodged on 4.4.2023.
Merely because, there is some delay in lodging the complaint, it cannot be the ground to reject the claim petition.
19. It is true that, in Ex.R1-MLC register, it has been recorded that "RTA fall from the Bike by hitting divider at 7.45 p.m."
But in police intimation marked at Ex.P14 clearly mentioned that "RTA fall from the Bike by hitting container at 7.45 p.m. on 3.4.2023 at nice road, Gollaratte (KA-05-AH-1189 container vehicle No).
MLC register and police intimation written by hospital authorities.
To substantiate the case of the respondent No.2, has not examined neither author of the document nor I.O. or any independent eye witness to prove its case.
No doubt, Ex.R1 marked with consent.
Mere marking of a document by consent by itself cannot be taken that the contents of the said documents stands proved in its entirety.

On perusal of Ex.R1 MLC extract it appears the hospital authorities Nitish.L vs Balaagavi Traders on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6479245/
4 have made mistakes while writing history of patient.
The victim cannot suffer, the mistakes done by the hospital authorities.

20. Apart from this, PW1 was subjected to cross- examination at length, but nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW1 that this accident is not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Even in the cross-examination of RW1, no material answers culled out from his mouth to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Except making allegations, the respondent No.2 has not placed any reliable documents to show that the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.

21. In the light of the oral evidence of the PW1 coupled with police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P8, it is clear that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident which is result of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05-AG-1189.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
22.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.

The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

23. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
Pain and Sufferings;

sentences.text: PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P5.

The said would certificate discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1.Lacerated wound over the right leg 2.Abrasion wound over the neck 25.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary and OPD at Ex.P9 and Ex.P11.
On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 issued by KIMS Hospital reveals that the petitioner was admitted from 4.4.2023 to 10.4.2023.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
26.
PW1 has stated that, he was studying B.Com., and also working part time in hotel as a supplier and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to show his income.
Hence, it is opt to be considered notional income.
On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 issued by KIMS Hospital reveals that the petitioner was admitted from 4.4.2023 to 10.4.2023.

By considering the nature of the injuries definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one month by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
27.
The petitioner has produced medical bills for Rs.33,937/- as per Ex.P10.
There are no contra materials available on record to show that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.
Therefore, the petitioenr is entitled for Rs.33,937/- under the head of medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
28.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food,
nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

sentences.text: 29. The petitioner herein asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.

Except the production of medical documents and averments made in the main petition as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor in order to prove the disability sustained by him due to the accidental injuries in order to know, whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner will effect to his future and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort to the petitioner to do his routine work as well as his work for his avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future income due to want of evidence on record.

Loss of amenities;
30.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he cannot do any manual work.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood as a mason.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
31. In connection with the future medication, the petitioner has not examined doctor to speak about future medication.
Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation of under the head of future medical expenses.

32. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs.25,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs.15,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.
Medical expenses Rs.33,937-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 8,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Nil due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs.20,000-00
7. Future medication Nil Total Rs.1,01,937-00 33.

34. As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the driver of Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-05-AH-1189 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
35. The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the TATA Goods Vehicle (Tr.).
In this regard respondent No.2 has examined legal executive as RW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
In the cross-examination he has clearly admitted that driver of the offending vehicle had licence to drive LMV can drive the container as the weight of the container is 2950 kgs.
Apart from this, as per charge sheet, the police have charge sheeted against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Except making allegations, has not placed any documents to impeach the recitals of charge sheet.
Hence, the defence taken by the respondent No.2 cannot be accepted.
Therefore, on perusal of the evidence of RW1 it is clear that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
36. As per records the policy was in force from 6.4.2022 to 5.4.2023.
The alleged accident occurred on 3.4.2024.
Hence, the respondent No.2 being the indemnifier of the respondent No.1 has to satisfy the award.

Therefore, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
37.

In view of above discussions on Issue Nos.1 to & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner u/ s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,01,937/- (Rupees one lakh one thousand nine hundred and thirty seven only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,01,937/- (Rupees one lakh one thousand nine hundred and thirty seven only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the amount is very meagre, entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
